Overview Webhooks enable Clay to automatically receive data from other applications through HTTP POST requests in JSON format whenever specific events occur. Your table updates instantly with new data, eliminating manual entry. This feature is particularly valuable for real-time updates, such as when adding new leads or modifying records based on external triggers. Creating a table with webhook In a workbook, click + Add at the bottom. Search for Webhooks and click Monitor webhook . Copy the URL/cURL. URL: Paste this URL into the application sending data to Clay. This URL is where your data will be sent. cURL: Paste the cURL command into your command line to send data directly to Clay. Optionally, add authentication token. To secure your webhook, include the authentication token in your request under the header key x-clay-webhook-auth . Make sure to copy the token immediately, as you can only access authentication tokens once. Optionally, add an idempotency key. Include a stable ID of 1 to 250 characters, such as an event ID or object ID, under the header key x-clay-webhook-idempotency-key . Repeated deliveries with the same idempotency key keep the latest payload instead of adding duplicate rows. Idempotency keys don't work on tables with auto-delete enabled. Note: Webhook sources are limited to 50,000 submissions, and this limit persists even after deleting rows. On Enterprise plans, you can enable Auto-delete (also called passthrough tables) so Clay processes and deletes rows automatically, letting one webhook receive unlimited submissions. On all other plans, you’ll need to create a new webhook once you hit 50,000 submissions to keep receiving data. ISO 27001 + Securely connect your CRM and other systems. ISO 42001 Securely connect your CRM and other systems. FAQ How do I pick the right plan? We've designed each plan around the features that fit where you are in your GTM journey. The best place to start is matching your needs to the right tier, not trying to predict your exact Data Credits or Action volumes. Here's what's included in each plan: Free — A low risk way to learn and experiment with Clay. Includes unlimited seats and tables, multi-provider waterfalls, Claygent enrichment, Clay Sequencer for email, and up to 200 rows per table. Comes with 100 Data Credits and 500 Actions/mo. Launch (starting at $185/mo) — The best way to start building in Clay. For individuals and small teams automating their first prospecting workflows. Includes everything in Free , plus phone number enrichment, job change and signal tracking, email campaign integrations, and up to 50,000 rows per table. Includes 2,500 Data Credits and 15,000 Actions/mo. Growth (starting at $495/mo) — For teams scaling their GTM motion. Includes everything in Launch , plus CRM auto-sync and enrichment, HTTP API integrations, webhook automation, web intent signal tracking, audience pushes to ads platforms, and priority support. Includes 6,000 Data Credits and 40,000 Actions/mo. Enterprise (custom pricing with annual commitment) — For GTM teams running at scale, with enterprise-grade security, support, and infrastructure. Includes everything in Growth , plus unlimited Audiences across sources, unlimited row bulk enrichment, Clay API access, data warehouse syncs, SSO, RBAC permissions management, additional Ads audiences, and a dedicated Growth Strategist. Includes 100,000+ Data Credits and 200,000+ Actions/mo. Every plan comes with a set number of Data Credits and Actions sized to cover the needs of most users at that tier. If you need more, you can top up Data Credits or step into a higher Action tier at any time. ‍ What are Actions and Data Credits? How do they work? Data Credits are used when you purchase data from Clay's marketplace — finding emails, phone numbers, company data across our 150+ data partners. Data credits always get cheaper as you grow. We've negotiated volume discounts directly with our data partners, passing those savings on to you. Clay is now both comparable to what you’d pay externally and meaningfully cheaper. If you bring your own API keys for third-party data, you skip Data Credit costs entirely and only use Actions for the platform work Clay handles behind the scenes. Actions measure the orchestration you do on Clay — enriching data, running a table, calling an AI model, sending data to a third-party system, or exporting data out of Clay. When you choose a plan, you're buying access to Clay's platform at a certain scale. Plans are sized based on real usage data, so the vast majority of customers have more than enough capacity for how they work in Clay. If you do reach your Action limit, you can upgrade to the next Action tier. ‍ Do unused Data Credits or Actions roll over? Actions reset each billing cycle and don’t roll over, since they reflect the platform capacity your plan includes. Each plan includes enough Actions to cover 90% of customer usage, and if you need more, you can increase your Action tier. Data Credits work more like a currency and do roll over. On Launch and Growth plans, unused credits can accumulate up to 2x your monthly credit amount (e.g., a 10,000 credit plan can bank up to 20,000 total). Enterprise customers can roll over up to 15% of their prior year's purchased credits, provided they renew at an equal or higher commitment. Why are Actions and Data Credits separate? Think of it as two separate things happening at once: Clay is doing work, and Clay is buying data on your behalf. Data Credits cover the cost of the data itself — the email address, phone number, or company detail sourced from one of Clay's 150+ data partners. Because we've negotiated volume discounts directly with our partners, we're able to pass those savings on to you, meaning you're getting comparable data prices through Clay to what you'd find going to most providers directly. Actions cover the platform work Clay does on your behalf — routing your request, calling the provider, running your workflow, and returning the result to your table. Actions cost less than a cent each and get cheaper with scale. If an enrichment returns no result, you're not charged Data Credits or Actions. If you bring your own API keys for a data provider, you skip Data Credits entirely and only use Actions for the platform work Clay handles behind the scenes. For more details, read the Action and Data Credits help doc . Will I have enough Actions and Data Credits on my plan? We have scoped out Launch and Growth plans so that 90% of our customers will never hit a usage limit. Users can always buy more if they need to top up without being pushed up to a higher plan tier. Enterprise customers will build custom plans with their GTMEs. The thresholds for each plan were selected carefully to give our customers enough room to experiment and iterate while reducing anxiety about how usage impacts spend. How much do Data Credits cost? Data Credits start at $0.05 each and become more cost-effective as you grow. Data is priced as competitively as possible. By negotiating volume discounts directly with our 150+ partners and passing those savings on to you, the most-used enrichments cost 50% fewer credits on average. How much do Actions cost? Actions start at less than $0.01 each and get cheaper with scale within each plan. ‍ How does AI usage work in Clay? Customers now have a choice between two pricing options for AI on Clay: Fixed-price: 80% of models in Clay continue to cost a flat number of Data Credits per task, including all of Clay’s native models. These are ideal for common tasks like classification, short summaries, templated content generation, and simple lookups. Variable: Token intensive models (e.g., GPT-5.1 and Claude 4.6 Sonnet) now have variable pricing based on actual token consumption. These models are best suited for multi-step research, complex Claygent prompts that synthesize across multiple sources, and detailed account-level analysis. Clay charges customers exactly for the tokens consumed with no markup. This means you’re getting access to frontier models at true cost. AI runs are 2x faster using Clay’s API keys compared to customers using their own because of the higher rate limits that Clay has negotiated with AI vendors. How can I tell if an AI model is fixed or variable? Variable models will show an estimated number of Data Credits per row, indicated by a tilde symbol (~). Final cost will be determined after the run completes, and usage data shows that 75% of runs cost less than the estimate. For more details, read the AI pricing help doc . ‍ Can I use my own API keys in Clay? Customers are still welcome to use their own API keys for data enrichment or AI in Clay. Each run will count as one Action, but no Data Credit will be used. AI runs are 2x faster using Clay’s API keys compared to customers using their own because of the higher rate limits that Clay has negotiated with AI vendors. Learn your way. ⌘ K ​ Open workspace ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ Log in Sign up ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Sign up to Clay Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers Docs index ​ ​ Overview ​ Courses ​ Docs ​ Use case templates ​ Certifications ​ Cohorts ​ Clay.com Doc Topics Getting started Find Enrich Transform Web scraping Gen AI Export Settings & admin Signals & triggers All docs / Gen AI / Clay MCP in ChatGPT Clay MCP in ChatGPT Connect the Clay MCP to ChatGPT, sign in to your workspace, and see what you can build and run from a chat on your plan. Overview The Clay MCP is a ChatGPT app that connects ChatGPT to your Clay workspace with your own Clay sign-in. Once it's set up, you can search Clay's GTM dataset, run your workspace's functions, and build multi-step workflows, email campaigns, and segments from a conversation, all on Clay's existing integrations and data. It carries the same tools as the Clay CLI, the clay command that coding agents run, packaged for chat. If you work in Claude Code or Codex instead, see Installing Clay Plugin (API & CLI) . ChatGPT lists two Clay apps. This doc covers the Clay MCP, listed as Clay . The other, listed as Clay for Reps , is MCP for Reps, which sales reps use to prospect and to run the functions their ops team approves; see Using Clay in ChatGPT for that one. Before you start You'll need: A ChatGPT account. If your company runs ChatGPT on a Business, Enterprise, or Edu plan, a ChatGPT admin may need to make Clay available to you first. Editor or Admin access in the Clay workspace you'll connect. Setting up the Clay MCP in ChatGPT Find Clay in ChatGPT's app directory. In ChatGPT, open the app directory, search for Clay, and connect the app named Clay , not Clay for Reps . Connect your workspace. When ChatGPT sends you to Clay, sign in, choose the workspace to connect, and click Authorize . Confirm it's working. Start a new chat with Clay turned on, and ask something like "Which Clay workspace am I connected to?" Troubleshooting You can't find or connect Clay on a company ChatGPT plan: a ChatGPT admin needs to make Clay available in your ChatGPT workspace. Clay shows No workspaces available , or your workspace isn't in the list: you need Editor or Admin access in that workspace. Ask a workspace admin to change your role. You connected the wrong workspace: disconnect Clay in ChatGPT's settings, then connect again and choose the right workspace. Some tools seem to be missing: ChatGPT only sees the tools your workspace role allows. Ask a workspace admin if you need more access. What you can do Ask for what you want in plain language, and ChatGPT picks the Clay tools to use. Search results, segments, campaigns, and workflows can show as interactive previews right in the chat. Searches Find companies and people with structured filters over Clay's GTM dataset, refine the search as you go, and see the results as a table in the chat. From the results table, you can run your workspace's functions on the rows you found. Results count toward your plan's search limits, covered in Plan availability and limits below. "Find Series B SaaS companies in the US with 100–500 employees." "Now narrow that to companies hiring for RevOps roles." "Find the VP of Sales at each of those companies." Audiences Work with Audiences, where your workspace's own people, companies, and deals live. You can look up records, count or search the records that match a filter, and create or edit segments of people and companies. "How many companies in our Audiences are in the healthcare segment?" "Show me the people we have at Acme Corp." Functions and routines Run Clay-managed functions and your own custom functions on a single record or in bulk. They run as routines, a function or workflow made callable from outside the Clay app, and you can save an existing function or workflow as a new routine from ChatGPT. You can start runs, check their status, and cancel them from the chat. "Which routines do we have for enriching companies?" "Run our company-scoring routine on Stripe." "What's the status of my last bulk run?" Workflows Note: Workflows is in beta. A Workspace Admin can request access from the Beta program section of your workspace settings by clicking Join beta program . Build and edit Workflows, Clay's builder for multi-step logic that runs one record at a time, for enrichment, research, scoring, routing, and other repeatable GTM work. You can run a test, rerun failed runs, read the results step by step, set alerts, and publish a workflow when it's ready. ChatGPT can show the workflow and its recent runs in the chat. "Build a workflow that takes a company domain, finds the head of marketing, and scores fit against our ICP." "Test it on these five domains." "Why did yesterday's runs fail at the enrichment step?" Tables Read data from your Clay tables: list tables, look at their columns, read rows, and ask questions about a table's data, like counts and totals. Tables are read-only from ChatGPT, so to build new logic, ask for a workflow instead. Listing tables and reading rows need a paid or trial plan. Queries that combine several tables need API table sync, available on Enterprise plans. "Show me the first 20 rows of our Inbound Leads table." Sequencer Build and edit campaign sequences in Sequencer, Clay's email outreach tool. You can check copy for spam triggers, send a test email, run variant tests, and read analytics, and ChatGPT can show the campaign in the chat after an edit. Launching, pausing, and resuming a campaign stay in the Clay app. "Draft a 3-step sequence for the VP of Sales list we just built." "How is the Q4 outbound campaign performing?" Signals Create and manage signals, which watch your accounts and contacts for changes such as job changes, new hires, and funding news. You can also edit, pause, resume, or delete a signal. "Watch our target accounts for funding news." Plan availability and limits The Clay MCP is available on every Clay plan, including Free and Trial. Search result limits are shared across the Clay MCP, the CLI, and Clay's Public API, and they scale with your plan: Plan Results per request Results per search Results per period Free 50 50 100 per 30 days Trial 50 50 10,000 per 14 days Flex 500 Up to your period limit 50,000 per 30 days Paid self-serve plans 500 Up to your period limit 1,000,000 per 30 days Legacy paid plans 500 Up to your period limit 1,000,000 per year Enterprise 500 Up to your period limit 10,000,000 per 30 days Results per request is the most one page of search results can hold. Results per search is the total you can page through for one search, and results per period is your workspace's running total across the Clay MCP, the CLI, and the Public API together. 30-day periods roll rather than resetting on a set date: each day at midnight UTC, the oldest day of usage ages out of the window. Legacy paid plans (Starter, Explorer, and Pro) keep a yearly period that resets on January 1 UTC instead. Moving to a current paid plan or to Enterprise switches the workspace to the rolling window. When you go over a limit, Clay tells you which limit you hit, and a period-limit message also says when usage frees up. On Free and Trial, the message links to upgrading your plan. To raise a limit on any other plan, contact Clay Support; Enterprise workspaces can reach out to their Clay account team. Checking your search usage Open the API and CLI page in the left sidebar. The Search usage card shows the results your workspace has used out of its limit for the current period, including searches run from ChatGPT. A rolling 30-day period shows Counts the last 30 days , and a fixed period shows the date it resets. FAQs Does using the Clay MCP cost extra? No. Work you start from ChatGPT spends the same credits and actions as the same work done in the Clay app. That spend is reported as MCP usage for the person who ran it, rather than as API and CLI usage. What's the difference between the Clay MCP and MCP for Reps? They cover different use cases, so ChatGPT has a separate app for each. The Clay MCP is for builders who want to work in Clay without leaving ChatGPT. It signs you in with your own Clay account and gives you the tools your workspace role allows, so you can build workflows, query Audiences, edit campaigns, and more. MCP for Reps is for sales reps to prospect with. Reps can find people and companies and run the functions and workflows that admins and editors have enabled for them, and an admin sets each rep's credit budget. See MCP in Clay for how that access is configured, and Clay MCP for Reps vs. Agent Plugin for choosing between the rep and builder surfaces. Can a workspace admin control who uses Clay from ChatGPT? Yes. On the Agent users page, which admins open from the sidebar on the Clay homepage, the Allowed MCP clients section has a toggle for each AI app. Turning ChatGPT off blocks ChatGPT from connecting to the workspace, and anyone who tries sees Not permitted by your workspace . Access also follows each person's role. Clay checks it on every request, so removing someone from the workspace or lowering their role below Editor cuts off their ChatGPT access right away. It's the same role check the CLI uses, covered in CLI security and privacy .
